newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady with a firm tone as harvesting continues to curtail marketings, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to Iowa and southern Minnesota plants could range from $58.50 to $59.00 per cwt while Illinois prices could match Wednesday's top of $58.00 at the plant, they said. USDA reported a top in Illinois at $57.00 but private sources said up to $58.00 had been paid.
Indiana and Ohio top prices at the plant could range from $56.00 to $57.50, unchanged from Wednesday as marketings in those areas keep up with demand, sources in those areas said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota marketings were lighter than expected Tuesday and seen light Wednesday as farmers dodged scattered rain showers and concentrated on getting as much harvesting done as possible.
The run Tuesday came in at 89,000 head, according to USDA, well below the day's estimate of 105,000. Wednesday's estimate was 100,000 head.
Pork prices at midday were mixed in slow trading, with skinned hams weak, bellies generally steady and lean trimmings higher in a light test, according to USDA's carlot pork report.
